domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain focuses heavily on common occupational skills and professional practices, representing an assigned weight percent of 11.2 on the broad certification evaluation for all candidates taking the test.
This section covers preparing and assembling tube, tubing and pipe completely, representing a defined weight percent of 10.4 of the total questions on the exam administered across the nation.
This domain addresses sewers, sewage treatment systems, and drainage, waste and vent systems with a substantial weight percent of 25.6 across the entire test designed for plumbing professionals.

This area covers water service and distribution installations, testing procedures, and servicing requirements, making up a significant 19.2 percent of the overall evaluation administered by provincial and territorial authorities.

This content involves plumbing fixtures, appliances, and water treatment systems, representing a distinct weight percent of 13.6 of the total questions found on the assessment for trade qualification certification.

This subject domain covers low-pressure steam and hydronic systems completely, featuring a designated weight percent of 12.8 on the formal interprovincial trade qualification exam taken by certified journeypersons.

This final domain focuses strictly on specialized systems, accounting for 7.2 percent of the overall exam content and testing advanced technical knowledge required in the modern plumbing trade across Canada.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at the testing center early with your government-issued photo ID and any required administrative documentation. Manage your 240 minutes carefully while checking your bubble sheet numbers frequently to ensure maximum accuracy.

faq.answer_text: The exam consists of 125 multiple-choice questions. Each question is worth one mark, and candidates have a total writing time of 240 minutes to complete the test booklet and bubble sheet.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The passing score for the exam is 70%. Candidates must meet or exceed this percentage to achieve a passing grade and obtain trade certification through their provincial authority.
The exam allows for a writing time of 240 minutes. Candidates should pace themselves across the 125 questions to ensure they have enough time to review their bubble sheet.

Candidates must bring required items such as government-issued photo ID and proof of apprenticeship. Check with your provincial or territorial apprenticeship office for specific administrative rules before exam day.
faq.question_title: What should I bring to the exam room?

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the Red Seal Plumber Exam with 125 questions over 240 minutes. Covers 7 major work activities for Canadian trade certification.

methodology.summary: Editorial content is carefully compiled using verified facts and official exam documentation from the Red Seal program to provide accurate, reliable guidance for candidates.

editorial.overview: The Red Seal Plumber Exam is formally administered through the Interprovincial Standards Red Seal Program to evaluate required competencies for professional plumbing across Canada. Candidates must complete a set of 125 multiple-choice questions within a strict time limit of 240 minutes to successfully achieve the national passing score of 70% required for full trade certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the Red Seal Occupational Standard very carefully before your test date. Candidates should use sticky notes for important plumbing procedures and study all national mathematical formulas alongside code book layouts. Check your knowledge effectively using the official self-assessment tool and focus your preparation exclusively on areas with lower confidence levels before finally writing.

editorial.who_should_take: Journeypersons and experienced apprentices seeking trade certification. Candidates must have practical work experience across the full scope of plumbing trade activities as determined by their provincial or territorial apprenticeship and certification authority.
